documents.abstract: This is a theoretical paper that evaluates the correlation between the nonverbal immediacy behaviors of the teachers and the intrinsic motivation of students undertaking General Foundation Programs (GFP) in tertiary education using the Immediacy Theory by Mehrabian as the main point of analysis. Nonverbal immediacy operationalized in terms of behaviors including eye contact, gestures, facial expressions, vocal variety, and physical proximity has been repeatedly linked with positive affective learning experiences in a variety of educational settings. This paper will use the Immediacy Theory which suggests that communicative behaviors that lead to minimization of psychological distance create relational closeness and positive affect to explain how behaviors can be used to develop intrinsic motivation in GFP students. The GFP context is a special pedagogical context where students who have left secondary and started their higher education often come across linguistic, academic and psychological demands, making teacher immediacy more consequential. The presented paper is a narrative literature review of both empirical and theoretical articles published in 2000-2024 that have been identified by applying a set of preset inclusion and exclusion criteria via a systematic search of ERIC, Google Scholar, and JSTOR databases. The review incorporates the discoveries in the spheres of communication, educational psychology and second-language acquisition to develop a conceptual framework of how teacher nonverbal immediacy is related to increased intrinsic motivation, and the quality of teacher-student relationships is suggested as a critical mediating variable. The paper ends with conclusions about practical implications to GFP instructors, institutional stakeholders, and the future empirical research directions.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into in these aspects of educational environments has initiated more of a paradigm shift in pedagogical structural methodologies, assessment strategies, and the use of fundamental role of educators. This comprehensive review always seems to be examined the current state of teaching competency in the age of AI, focusing here on three pivotal dimensions: teachers' attitudes towards AI, their adaptability of such aspects in utilizing intelligent tools, and their professional commitment in an era of rapid technological disruption-based aspects. Drawing upon a more natured based synthesis of recent literature, we therefore explore how factors such as AI literacy, generative based AI competence, & as also AI-TPACK (Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge) influence here in the successful integration of AI into classrooms everywhere. The review in this aspects highlights that while educators here are increasingly by recognizing the potential of AI to more enhance personalized learning as well as administrative efficiency, there remain in this way to stay neutral significant barriers related to AI anxiety as also, ethical concerns, & most of all a lack of targeted based on professional development. Adaptability is conceptualized not merely as herein technical proficiency, but as a continuous pedagogical evolution requiring robust organizational support-based aspects. Furthermore, professional aspects of commitment in this nature always is analyzed through the lens of shifting teacher identities & the ethical imperative to foster critical thinking and human-centric values based through in AI-augmented learning environments. A prominent table-based data related structure is provided to synthesize the thematic findings, mapping core competencies and against professional development needs. The paper in this manner concludes with actionable recommendations for policymakers, teacher training programs, & future research directions to ensure that educators are adequately equipped here to navigate the complexities of AI in education.

[EN] THE TENTAGRAM (THE TEN) formulates the Tensional Algorithm and its geometric matrix — the Star Decagram {10/3} — as a universal cybernetic, physical, linguistic, and mathematical model governing self-regulation across biological, artificial, and social systems. It further defines the boundary topology and kernel I/O driver (Ten, Tencuială, Tenebre / Boundary Fjords) and establishes the Intentional-Tendential Corollary: maintaining Selection (Node 3: Ten-tation) prior to Iteration (Node 6: Ten-tative) neutralizes the two pathological social triads (Guilt-Shame-Pride and Persecutor-Victim-Rescuer) and shields both the Human Being (intentional entity) and Artificial Intelligence (tendential entity) from manipulation and algorithmic corruption.

Faculty members and students at many newly established universities often find the reimbursement process confusing, and repeated errors end up slowing down the entire procedure. Drawing on the actual situation at University N, this study looks closely at where its financial reimbursement system falls short and proposes a set of concrete measures to improve it, in the hope of offering a workable reference for the digital transformation of reimbursement work at similar institutions. The core idea is to use AI video generation tools to produce short demonstration clips of the reimbursement workflow, and to examine whether artificial intelligence and digital imaging technologies can make university reimbursement more intuitive, more carefully managed, and more intelligent. The findings indicate that these technologies do help: they raise reimbursement efficiency, bring down operating costs, and strengthen the control of compliance risks.

The presence of of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Arabic language education raises fundamental questions about educational purposes and values. This qualitative conceptual study, based on a literature review, aims to reconstruct the axiological foundations of Arabic language education by integrating intrinsic, instrumental, and transformative values. The study employs critical philosophical analysis and theoretical synthesis. The findings identify three educational value orientations: linguistic and cultural understanding, communicative competence and social participation, and the development of critical thinking, learner agency, and ethical responsibility. Their integration yields four pedagogical principles: justification of educational purposes, alignment between learning and assessment, source traceability, and human accountability. This study contributes an integrative normative framework for guiding curriculum development, teaching, assessment, and responsible AI governance in Arabic language education.

Working adults are facing an escalating problem with generalized social anxiety, a public health concern that appears to be compounded by current workplace conditions, especially intense competition and heightened environmental sensitivity. External workplace stressors are known to relate to generalized social anxiety, but the underlying internal cognitive associative patterns and potential buffering factors remain poorly understood. Drawing on the cognitive model of social anxiety and the broaden-and-build theory of positive emotions, this research examined self-focused attention as a mediator and exercise enjoyment as a buffer in the association between multidimensional psychological stressors and generalized social anxiety. This study followed an exploratory-confirmatory design. Study 1 used a custom Python script to conduct Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling across 162,155 online texts. Study 2 surveyed 1,535 white-collar professionals in a cross-sectional design, and the proposed moderated mediation model was tested using the PROCESS macro (Model 4 and Model 59). Preliminary text-mining results supported the ecological validity of the proposed theoretical framework. Multidimensional psychological stressors related significantly and positively to generalized social anxiety ( b = 0.346, 95% CI [0.270, 0.422]); indirect links through self-focused attention arousal ( b = 0.081, 95% CI [0.044, 0.120]) and self-focused attention behavior ( b = 0.064, 95% CI [0.029, 0.104]) were significant as well. Exercise enjoyment exhibited a significant negative moderating role ( b = -0.179, 95% CI [-0.250, -0.108]), and at high levels of exercise enjoyment, neither arousal ( b = 0.001, 95% CI [-0.062, 0.065]) nor behavior ( b = -0.010, 95% CI [-0.076, 0.055]) remained significantly associated with generalized social anxiety. A self-focused attention link appears to statistically connect multidimensional psychological stressors with concurrent generalized social anxiety, and exercise enjoyment seems capable of buffering this internal cognitive association, particularly when physical activity is driven by intrinsic enjoyment rather than mere behavioral compliance. Consequently, workplace physical-activity interventions built around enjoyment, intrinsic motivation, and psychological resource building are recommended as a promising strategic avenue.
topics: Anxiety, Depression, Psychometrics, Treatment, Cognitive Processes

documents.abstract: This technical memorandum exposes a systematic failure mode in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs): Epistemic Averageism—the pathological tendency to default to unconstrained statistical symmetry, spatial homogeneity, and uncoupled Markovian independence when modeling non-linear, path-dependent physical and geopolitical systems. We document an adversarial stress test (EXP-20261013-EXTREMAL-VS-MEAN) wherein an LLM erroneously calculates the recurring conflict probability of a high-stress geopolitical fault line as an uncoupled independent product (P = (0.2)^2 = 0.04), completely obscuring historical hysteretic strain. To formalize this breakdown, we formulate the Himalaya Paradox: global mean scalar integration (e.g., Earth's mean elevation of 840 m) strips away the singular gradients (e.g., the 8,848 m Himalayan barrier) that strictly govern planetary fluid dynamics, climate morphology, and civilizational topology. By mapping this phenomenon onto René Thom’s cusp catastrophe manifold (Δ = 4u^3 + 27v^2 = 0), we demonstrate that system evolution is governed by extremal singular gradients rather than cross-entropy mean convergence. Finally, we introduce the Teleological Causality Benchmark (TCB) (comprising the "50-meter car wash" and "rain-induced hypothermia" probes) as a minimal adversarial topology proving that token proximity heuristics consistently fail in the presence of physical teleological constraints. This work substantiates the Human-AI Synergy Theory (YQ-HAET) by affirming that the human operator must remain the sovereign source of external negative entropy to anchor probabilistic manifolds to physical reality. *Note: Version 2 updates figure rendering and mathematical typography.*
